I've been farming these 10 mu for 20 years now. My father farmed here before me, and I've seen good years and bad years. At 70, I don't move as fast as I used to, but my youngest son still lives with us and helps out, especially during harvest. My wife and I do most of the daily work.

**Winter wheat**

I plant wheat on all 10.1 mu — that's our main crop, and we need the grain both for selling and for our own flour. I always plant around October 10th, give or take a few days depending on when the rain comes. This year I'll use the same improved wheat seed I bought from the village supply store last year. It costs about 45 yuan per mu, which is a bit steep, but my neighbor Lao Zhang used cheaper seed two years ago and his yield was poor, so I stick with what works.

For fertilizer, I put down a base of compound fertilizer before planting — about 50 jin per mu. That's what I've always done. Then in the spring, when the wheat starts turning green around Qingming, I topdress with urea. Last year I used about 40 jin of urea per mu at jointing, and the yield was decent, around 450 jin per mu. This year fertilizer prices are still high, so I'm thinking of cutting back a little on the topdress — maybe 35 jin per mu instead of 40. But I'm worried about that because if I cut too much and the weather turns dry, I'll lose more than I save. I'll probably end up doing about 40 jin like last year. Better to waste a little money than risk a bad harvest. In total, that's roughly 18 kg of nitrogen per mu across both applications.

I irrigate three times for wheat: once after planting to help it germinate and settle in for winter, once in the spring at jointing, and once at heading if it doesn't rain. Each time costs me about 15-20 yuan per mu for the electricity to pump from the well. The well water is getting more expensive, so I watch the sky closely. If it rains in the spring, I skip the jointing irrigation. But you can't count on rain.

I spray herbicide once in the spring — the weeds here are stubborn. That's about 25 yuan per mu. I don't usually need insecticide for wheat, but I'll keep an eye out.

**Summer maize**

After we harvest the wheat around June 8th, we have maybe 5-6 days to get the maize in the ground. Last year we were slow and planted on June 15th, which was a bit late. This year I want to plant by June 12th if the wheat dries quickly enough. We might hire a custom harvester for the wheat to save those two days — it costs about 60 yuan per mu, but getting the maize in early is worth it.

I use hybrid maize seed — about 55 yuan per mu. I buy it every year; saved seed doesn't grow well for maize.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting — about 40 jin per mu. Then I topdress with urea at the big-flush stage, around 30 jin per mu. That's about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu total. My neighbor's son went to agricultural college and told him to do 20 kg, but that's too much for my pocket. I'm not running a big business farm — I'm just trying to feed my family and have some cash left.

Maize irrigation depends on the rain. If it's a wet summer, maybe once. If it's dry like two years ago, twice. Each irrigation is another 15-20 yuan per mu. I usually don't irrigate maize more than twice — the water bill adds up too fast.

I spray herbicide once after planting, and sometimes I need to spray for corn borer if I see damage. That's another 20 yuan per mu.

**Labor and costs**

My son and I do most of the work. My wife helps with fertilizer spreading and weeding. For wheat harvest and maize planting, those 5-6 days are killers — we might hire two laborers for 2-3 days each, at about 120 yuan per day. Same for maize harvest in September. All told, maybe 1 hired day per mu across the year, but concentrated in June and September.

I'm watching my cash closely. Total input costs for both crops will be around 750-800 yuan per mu, so roughly 8,000 yuan for the whole farm. That's a lot of money for us. If wheat prices stay at 2.4 yuan per jin and maize at 1.2 yuan per jin, I should be able to cover costs and have some left, but there's no room for mistakes. One bad drought or one pest outbreak and we're in trouble.

I expect about 450 kg per mu for wheat and 500 kg per mu for maize if the weather cooperates. That's what I usually get, and I'm not expecting miracles.
